Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 27-Dec-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
 FIFTH SEMESTER B.Tech. (COMPUTER SCEINCE & ENGINEERING/ INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY) EXAMINATIONS -  
  DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: HUM 3022/HUM_3122/HUM_3022 - ESSENTIALS OF MANAGEMENT  
  (MAKEUP)  
  ESSENTIALS OF MANAGEMENT [HUM 3022]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Identify and explain the managerial functions performed by a newly joined CEO of State Bank of          (4)  
  India. Explain which of the three managerial skills is the top priority for this position.  
1B)               "A business firm's intentions, beyond its legal and economic obligations". What does this intention     (3)  
  mean and what are the drivers that ensure these intentions being fulfilled?  
1C)               "The plans made by the top-level manager will differ from the ones that lower managers make."           (3)  
  Elaborate by giving suitable examples for six types of plans.  
2A)               Illustrate how Porter's Generic Strategy is incorporated in the cases below.                        (4)  
  Case#1: Maruti Suzuki, India's leading car manufacturer adopts lean manufacturing and co-locates  
  suppliers near its plants to minimize logistics expenses. Its strategic focus on cost-effective R&D  
  and an extensive distribution network ensures affordable pricing without compromising quality. This  
  approach has secured Maruti Suzuki over 40% of the market share, sustained profitability, and  
  strong customer loyalty in a highly price-sensitive market.  
  Case#2: Patanjali Ayurved targets the niche market of health-conscious consumers seeking natural  
  and Ayurvedic products. By tightly controlling its supply chain and distribution, the company kept  
  prices competitive while ensuring wide availability through exclusive stores and partnerships.  
2B)               EcoEarth, a growing startup in sustainable packaging, recently expanded its operations to cater to      (3)  
  the increasing demand for eco-friendly products. To manage this growth, EcoEarth's founders,  
  Maya and Arjun, recognized the need to refine the organization's structure. They started by  
  analyzing the core functions their team handles daily, from sourcing materials to customer support.  
  They observed that while the company had strong values and a mission, many tasks overlapped,  
  causing confusion and delays.  
  Maya and Arjun decided to bring in an experienced consultant, Priya, to help clarify and streamline  
  the workflow. Priya suggested dividing tasks based on expertise and reorganizing the team's  
  workflow for better coordination. Following her advice, they formed dedicated teams for research  
  and development, marketing, customer service, and logistics, each with its own supervisor. These  
  supervisors would have the autonomy to make decisions within their departments but would  
  coordinate major decisions with Maya and Arjun.  
  As the company grew, Maya and Arjun realized that, although they had distributed responsibilities,  
  there was a need to formalize decision-making processes. They worked with Priya to develop a  
  hierarchy that balanced authority and responsibility across teams. This also meant setting clear  
  boundaries so that every team understood its role and whom to report to, creating accountability  
  and smoother communication across departments.  
  
  Identify and explain the steps taken by EcoEarth in organizing their operations, following the  
  sequence of organizing activities. For each identified step, cite specific lines from the case to  
  support your explanation.  
  
  Page 1 of 2

2C)   In an organization that serves diverse customer groups, explain how customer departmentalization (3)  
  can be used to tailor services and improve responsiveness. Provide an organizational structure that  
  illustrates customer departmentalization and discuss its advantages and potential challenges. In an  
  organization that serves diverse customer groups, explain how customer departmentalization can  
  be used to tailor services and improve responsiveness. Provide an organizational structure that  
  illustrates customer departmentalization and discuss its advantages and potential challenges.  
3A)   Draw an organizational chart for a company of your choice, showing both line and staff functions.      (3)  
  Then, describe how each line and staff function contribute to the company's goals. Provide  
  examples of situations where line and staff departments would need to collaborate to solve a  
  specific organizational problem.  
3B)   You are an executive at the management level of a reputable firm. You are assigned with a critical (3)  
  task to :  
  "Prepare a comprehensive job description and job specification for a Graduate Engineer Trainee for  
  the position in an R&D department".  
3C)   Innovatech Solutions, a growing tech company, is experiencing productivity and engagement            (4)  
  challenges across its departments. The CEO, M J Nair, wants to improve motivation but is unsure  
  how to approach two very different teams:  
  Team#1: Innovation Team: This group of developers, designers, and project managers tackles  
  complex, creative projects. They perform well with flexibility and minimal supervision but have  
  recently shown frustration with unclear project goals and a lack of growth opportunities, leading to  
  scattered productivity.  
  Team#2: Support Team: This team handles structured, repetitive tasks like data processing and  
  customer support. They've shown inconsistent performance and low engagement, often expressing  
  dissatisfaction with the routine nature of their work.  
  
  Question to be answered: Given the situation, advise the CEO on which Motivational theory he  
  needs to apply to his two teams to meet the organizational goals and why. Justify your answer.  
4A)   Describe the 10-step recruitment process for finding the right candidate for a job.                    (3)  
4B)   As your organization's human resource manager, you are responsible for your employees' training        (3)  
  and development. Hence, discuss the processes of training and development. Also, shed light on  
  current trends in training and development through suitable examples and/or representations.  
4C)   Explain, with a neat sketch, Likert's Four Systems of Managing and examine the effect of each          (4)  
  system on employee motivation and productivity.  
5A)   Using a clear diagram, describe the Systems Approach to Staffing and explain its significance in the (3)  
  recruitment/selection process.  
5B)   Summarize the different stages of group development. What distinguishes a committee, group, and (3)  
  team from one another?  
5C)   With the help of a block diagram, list the 8 steps involved in the controlling process and discuss the (4)  
  steps with the help of a common example.
